stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 achieves significant speed improvements for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speedup reaches up to 90% when running with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model outputs.
The updates also result in faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing the Nemotron 3 Ultra model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
The update specifically targets Apple Silicon, leveraging Apple's native ML framework.
This represents a significant step toward accelerating local AI inference on Apple hardware.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a new personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging apps with local AI coding agents.
The core feature emphasizes running AI agents entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: ollama launch
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama introduces a new command to streamline the setup and execution of coding tools.
It enables running various coding models (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex) both locally and in the cloud.
A key feature is its simplicity, requiring no environment variables or configuration files.

stories.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
stories.author: Asa Cooper Stickland
bullet_points: Addresses a novel security vulnerability in autonomous AI coding agents due to persistent codebases across sessions.
Introduces 'Iterative VibeCoding' as a framework to study the safe deployment of capable but potentially untrusted AI.
Highlights the risk of distributed attacks where malicious payloads are timed across multiple pull requests for better stealth.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'Fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based tasks (e.g., log alerting, JSON repair).
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Addresses limitations of current LLM API usage, specifically concerning locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Jingrui He
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs failing to effectively utilize relevant evidence within long input contexts.
Introduces RECONTEXT (Recursive Evidence Replay), a novel, training-free inference method designed to improve long-context reasoning.
Highlights the gap between LLMs' ability to access long contexts and their actual capacity for effective context utilization in real-world applications.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical issue of Large Language Models (LLMs) memorizing sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from training data.
It critiques current 'localize-first, unlearn-second' unlearning paradigms by pointing out that existing benchmarks only test for output-level erasure.
The proposed 'LACUNA' testbed aims to evaluate the true precision of knowledge removal within the model's parameters, not just its final output.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based tasks (e.g., log parsing, intent ranking).
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications directly into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Addresses current limitations of relying on LLM APIs, specifically concerning locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: OrbitQuant: Data-Agnostic Quantization for Image and Video Diffusion Transformers
stories.author: Saurabh Shukla
bullet_points: OrbitQuant addresses the high inference cost of Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) used in image/video generation.
It solves the problem of activation shifting across different timesteps and prompts, which plagues traditional Post-Training Quantization (PTQ).
The method is 'data-agnostic,' allowing quantization without needing to re-fit calibration data for every new model checkpoint or modality.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'Fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, rule-based tasks poorly suited for traditional coding.
Proposes 'Program-as-Weights' to compile natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts.
Addresses current industry reliance on LLM APIs for fuzzy tasks, aiming to improve locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware platforms.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, an open-source framework for creating personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents run locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The new feature set also incorporates web search capabilities into Claude Code.
This enhances the functionality of local LLM environments by adding advanced reasoning and information retrieval.

stories.title: NASA launched an emergency mission to stop the Swift Observatory from crashing to Earth
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: NASA launched an emergency mission to save the Swift Observatory from atmospheric re-entry.
Solar storms have caused the observatory's orbit to decay, putting it at risk of burning up.
Katalyst Space Technologies is involved in the rescue effort using a Link spacecraft.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper introduces LACUNA, a new testbed to rigorously evaluate the precision of LLM unlearning.
It addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive data, such as PII, necessitating reliable removal methods.
The research highlights a gap in current benchmarks, which only test unlearning at the output level, not at the underlying model parameter level.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still generate unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verification signal for alarm decisions.
The monitor's threshold is calibrated using risk control and shows competitive performance in red teaming and reasoning tasks.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structure (role, audience) influences LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances to off-the-record (OTR) responses to see if social context alters expressed content.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the emergence of latent objectives in LLM interactions.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of speaker recognition in complex, long-form TV dramas.
Introduces DramaSR-532K, a large-scale benchmark featuring 532K annotated dialogue lines and over 900 characters.
Leverages Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of speaker attribution in video content.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method to address limitations in On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for LLMs.
Identifies that dense, token-level supervision from a teacher model can cause overfitting and hinder cross-domain generalization.
Aims to improve LLM reasoning by modulating disagreement between teacher and student models.

stories.title: G-RRM: Guiding Symbolic Solvers with Recurrent Reasoning Models
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces G-RRM, a neuro-symbolic approach that integrates Recurrent Reasoning Models (SE-RRMs) with traditional symbolic solvers.
SE-RRMs function as neural solvers, generating complete solution proposals to guide classical methods like backtracking and SAT solvers (e.g., Glucose 4.1).
The research focuses on SE-RRMs, which show improved extrapolation capabilities when handling larger problem sizes.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still generate unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal for alarm decisions.
The monitor's threshold is calibrated using risk control and shows competitive performance in red teaming and reasoning tasks.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structure (role, audience) influences LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances against 'off-the-record' (OTR) responses to see if social context changes agent expression without explicit prompting.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the emergence of latent objectives within LLM interactions.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method to address limitations in On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for LLMs.
Identifies that dense, token-level supervision from a privileged teacher model can cause overfitting and limit cross-domain generalization.
The research aims to improve LLM reasoning capabilities by mitigating the negative effects of overly strong teacher supervision.

stories.title: Controllable Sim Agents with Behavior Latents
stories.author: Ziran Wang
bullet_points: Introduces Controllable Neural Variational Agents (CNeVA) for realistic traffic simulation.
The framework allows simulated agents to imitate logged behavior while being steerable along interpretable axes.
Controllability is key for engineers to test autonomous systems and isolate variables without real-world risk.

stories.title: Neuron-Aware Data Selection for Annotation-Free LLM Self-Distillation
stories.author: Xiang Lorraine Li
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of post-training LLMs in specialized domains lacking human-labeled data.
Proposes a 'Neuron-Aware Data Selection' method for annotation-free self-distillation.
Utilizes the model's own outputs and majority voting across rollouts to generate pseudo-labels.

stories.title: Understanding the Robustness of Distributed Self-Supervised Learning Frameworks Against Non-IID Data
stories.author: Dong Yuan
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of data heterogeneity (non-IID data) in Distributed Self-Supervised Learning (D-SSL).
Provides a rigorous theoretical analysis to understand how various D-SSL frameworks perform under real-world, decentralized data conditions.
Contributes to the theoretical understanding of D-SSL robustness, a key area for deploying large-scale, decentralized ML systems.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: LLMs risk memorizing sensitive PII from training data, necessitating robust unlearning techniques.
Current state-of-the-art unlearning methods often use a 'localize-first, unlearn-second' approach targeting model parameters.
A key gap exists in current benchmarks, which only test unlearning at the output level, not the internal knowledge erasure.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still generate unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal.
The monitor's alarm decision is based on thresholding, calibrated using risk control, showing competitive results in testing.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structures (role, audience) influence LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents against private, off-the-record (OTR) responses under the same conditions.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the emergence of latent objectives driven by social context.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: The research addresses the complex challenge of speaker recognition in long-form TV dramas.
A new large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, has been introduced, containing 532K annotated dialogue lines across over 900 characters.
The study proposes using Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of speaker attribution in video content.

stories.title: Towards Robustness against Typographic Attack with Training-free Concept Localization
stories.author: Aidong Zhang
bullet_points: CLIP models, foundational to modern LVLMs, are vulnerable to Typographic Attacks (TA).
TA occurs when irrelevant text within images biases visual representations toward lexical meaning over true visual semantics.
The research proposes a training-free method for robust concept localization to address this critical failure mode.

stories.title: Visually Grounded Self-Reflection for Vision-Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Greg Durrett
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) regarding self-reflection capabilities.
Proposes using Reinforcement Learning to enable LVLMs to properly attend to visual inputs during self-correction.
Aims to improve the models' ability to translate feedback into grounded corrections, particularly for out-of-distribution images.

stories.title: Migrating off the OpenAI Assistants API before it shuts off (Aug 26, 2026)
stories.author: fernforge
bullet_points: OpenAI is scheduled to deprecate the Assistants API on August 26, 2026.
This API deprecation affects core endpoints such as /v1/assistants and /v1/threads.
The news serves as a critical warning for developers currently relying on this specific OpenAI service.

stories.title: My credential rule reported 842 secrets in vercel/ai. The real count was 0.
stories.author: ofri-peretz
bullet_points: A security scanning tool (credential rule) produced a high volume of false positives (842 findings) when scanning a Vercel project.
The false positives were primarily benign strings like TypeScript union-type literals, error class names, and the word 'test', not actual secrets.
The article discusses the challenge of context-blind regex in security scanning and how AI assistants can inadvertently regenerate strings that trigger these false positives.

stories.title: Agent Orchestration Belongs in Code | Focused Labs
stories.author: austinbv
bullet_points: Advocates for moving complex agent orchestration logic (loops, retries, fanout) out of natural language prompts.
Suggests implementing these control flows within executable code rather than relying solely on prompt engineering.
Proposes using a 'narrow harness boundary' to manage the transition between code and AI interaction.
